sheet-2.description: Residential blocks on the south-east side of downtown Pleasantville, south of the Main Street business district, drawn at 50 ft to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points to the upper right. South Franklin Avenue crosses the sheet near its top and South Chester Avenue, South Hampton Court and South Lyons Court follow it in parallel; East Decatur Avenue and Tunis Avenue on the left, East Verona Avenue (labelled Atlantic City Boulevard below South Hampton Court) in the middle and East West Jersey Avenue (Milan) on the right cross them. Lenox Avenue, also lettered Church, ends at South Franklin Avenue. The blocks are almost entirely frame dwellings with small auto houses and garages, a few brick-veneered or brick-first-storey houses and two apartment buildings. St. Mark's Episcopal Church and its parish house stand on the block above South Franklin Avenue west of Lenox Avenue, and a small gasoline station sits at the corner of East Verona and South Franklin Avenues. A wooden approach to a street railway viaduct is shown entering the block above Lenox Avenue. The city line between Pleasantville and Egg Harbor Township is drawn as a dash-dot line across the blocks along South Hampton Court, so the lowest row of blocks lies partly outside the city. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are marked in the streets. The scale bar is printed inside the bottom block.
notes: Old South Chester Avenue is today's South Hampden Court, old South Hampton Court is today's Lyons Court and old South Lyons Court is today's Frankfort Avenue (by position; the modern South Chester Avenue is only a stub near East Washington Avenue).
St. Mark's Episcopal Church and parish house, heated by steam, lit by electricity.
Wooden approach to a street railway viaduct at the top of the sheet.
City of Pleasantville / Egg Harbor Township line drawn across the bottom blocks.

Single part, 50 ft. Turned (north to upper right). S. Franklin, S. Chester (now S. Hampden Ct), S. Hampton Ct (now Lyons Ct), S. Lyons Ct (now Frankfort Av) crossed by E. Decatur, Tunis, E. Verona (Atlantic City Blvd), Lenox, E. West Jersey (Milan). St Marks Episcopal Church. City/township line.

sheet-3.description: The rail and utility corridor on the east side of downtown Pleasantville, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. South and North Franklin Avenue cross the upper half of the sheet and South and North Chester Avenue and South and North Hampton Court the lower half; East Washington Avenue runs down the middle from Madison Avenue at the top to South and North Lyons Court (South and North Clark Avenue) at the bottom. On the left, the electric and steam line of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad runs between the two halves of East West Jersey Avenue. On the right, the Philadelphia and Reading Railway (Atlantic City Division) runs beside East Grant Avenue (East Reading Avenue) with its passenger station, freight house and platforms, and a trolley trestle crosses at the top. East of the tracks lie the large industrial premises: the Taylor Packing Company plant of fireproof brick and concrete with auto and shipping platform, the Atlantic and Suburban Electric Railway Company car barns, the Hygienic Ice and Coal Company ice plant with storage and coal sheds on a wooden trestle, the Pleasantville Gas Company works with two gas holders, generator and meter rooms and tar tanks, and a Gulf Refining Company warehouse with gasoline tanks. Other buildings include a garage for 60 cars on East Washington Avenue, a water meter works, auto repair shops and a county tool house and repair shop; the remaining blocks are frame dwellings. Old Turnpike, North Franklin Avenue and Pennsylvania Avenue (Third Avenue) edge the right margin. The Pleasantville and Egg Harbor Township line crosses the bottom blocks.
notes: East West Jersey Avenue is drawn on both sides of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad; the east side street is today's Green Avenue, the west side keeps the name East West Jersey Avenue.
Old East Grant Avenue (East Reading Avenue) is today's Grant Avenue.

Modern East Washington Avenue north of Franklin, Madison Avenue and North Franklin Avenue east of Grant Avenue are realigned against the 1924 drawing; those junctions were excluded or carry 1.5 m residuals.
Taylor Packing Company plant, Atlantic and Suburban Electric Railway Company car barns, Hygienic Ice and Coal Company ice plant, Pleasantville Gas Company works, Gulf Refining Company warehouse.
Philadelphia and Reading Railway passenger station and freight house.

Single part, 50 ft, turned like sheet 2. E. Washington Av between Madison and Lyons Ct; W.J.&S. RR between the two E. West Jersey Avs (east one now Green Av); P&R Ry, E. Grant Av (now Grant Av), Old Turnpike. Taylor Packing Co, A&S Elec Ry car barns, ice plant, gas works.

sheet-4-1.description: Blocks east of the Old Turnpike on the north-east edge of downtown Pleasantville, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Madison Avenue runs along the top, North Franklin Avenue across the middle and Pennsylvania Avenue (3rd Street) below it; Old Turnpike forms the left edge, and Taubel Avenue, Charles Avenue and East Adams Avenue (right edge) cross them, with Hughes Avenue south of Pennsylvania Avenue. Troy Alley and 2nd Avenue are narrow lanes inside the blocks. The upper left block holds a Gulf Refining garage and repair shop with concrete walls and a paint shop, and the Pleasantville Gas Company's two gas holders and valve house. A hotel stands on Old Turnpike at 2nd Avenue. The rest is frame dwellings, many in rows of narrow lots, with auto houses and poultry houses; large blocks between Charles and East Adams Avenues are almost empty except for a foundation. The blocks south of Pennsylvania Avenue are laid out in narrow lots, largely unbuilt, and the city line between Pleasantville and Egg Harbor Township crosses their lower end. The lower right corner of the sheet is a separate inset (part 2).
notes: Old Taubel Avenue (20 to 30 ft wide) is today's Ingersoll Avenue; old 2nd Avenue is approximately today's Harris Avenue; the 20 ft alley between Old Turnpike and Taubel Avenue is followed by today's East Pleasant Avenue.
Pleasantville Gas Company gas holders; Gulf Refining garage and repair shop.
Madison Avenue is drawn with its south side only (70 ft); East Adams Avenue with its west side only.

Two parts, 50 ft, turned like sheet 2. Part 1 main: Madison, N. Franklin, Pennsylvania (3rd St) crossed by Old Turnpike, Taubel (now Ingersoll Av, 20-30 ft), Charles, E. Adams (edge). Gas holders, Gulf garage. Part 2: inset (heavy line, lower right) Clark Lumber Co on S./N. Lyons Ct below sheet 3; no junction, carried from sheet 3.

sheet-4-2.description: Inset in the lower right corner of sheet 4, framed by a heavy line and drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north to the upper right, showing the Clark Lumber Company lumber and mill work yard on the south side of South and North Lyons Court (South and North Clark Avenue), where East Washington Avenue meets it below sheet 3. The plant comprises a two-storey mill with mill work and bench work rooms, an office, a scale, a shaving vault fed by a blow pipe, a hydrant with hose, long lumber sheds, a cement storage building, warehouses, numbered lumber piles, a coal shed and brick and lumber storage. A railroad siding enters from the lower left and curves through the yard, with lumber platforms beside it and coal bins on a trestle. A note gives the average stock as 350,000 ft, a night watchman with clock, electric power and lights, steam heat with refuse fuel, town water and outside hydrants with 200 ft of hose. The surrounding area is marked no exposure.
notes: Clark Lumber Company, lumber and mill work.
No street junction survives in the inset; placed from sheet 3 (the end of East Washington Avenue at Lyons Court, marked by its water pipe) with sheet 3's scale and rotation: low confidence.
Old Lyons Court here does not match a modern street by name.

Two parts, 50 ft, turned like sheet 2. Part 1 main: Madison, N. Franklin, Pennsylvania (3rd St) crossed by Old Turnpike, Taubel (now Ingersoll Av, 20-30 ft), Charles, E. Adams (edge). Gas holders, Gulf garage. Part 2: inset (heavy line, lower right) Clark Lumber Co on S./N. Lyons Ct below sheet 3; no junction, carried from sheet 3.

sheet-5.description: The centre of Pleasantville's business district on Main Street, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. South Main Street crosses the sheet below the middle and continues to the right as North Main Street; Chestnut Street and South 2nd Street (Georgia Avenue) run along the top. West Verona Avenue (Beaumont Avenue) and East Verona Avenue form the left side, West and East West Jersey Avenue run beside the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad, Shore Fast Line, electric and steam) in the middle, and West and East Washington Avenue form the right side, with 1st Street and North 2nd Street leading off to the right. The railroad has a passenger station, a second station building, a switch tower, a freight depot and plank platforms. East of the tracks the Risley and Lake Company lumber yard fills the upper block with lumber sheds, lumber piles, coal pockets, a woodworking shop and an office and warehouse. Along Main Street stand brick and frame stores, the Pleasantville National Bank, the Pleasantville Trust Company bank, the First National Bank (fireproof construction, built 1924), a motion picture theatre, a bake house, a dress factory, a dampwash laundry, a hosiery dye house, an auto exchange, garages and auto repair shops, and The Gilmer boarding house on West West Jersey Avenue. Dwellings fill the outer blocks. At the bottom a street railway crosses on a steel viaduct with wooden approaches, beside a street railway ticket office.
notes: Old West Jersey Avenue jogs at Main Street (west side north of Main, east side south of it); the modern single node does not match the drawn junction and was excluded.
Risley and Lake Company lumber yard; Pleasantville National Bank; Pleasantville Trust Company; First National Bank built 1924; motion picture theatre.

West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Shore Fast Line, electric and steam) with stations, switch tower and freight depot; placed partly on the two grade crossings of today's Pleasantville Industrial Track.
Street railway steel viaduct with wooden approaches across the bottom of the sheet.

Single part, 50 ft, turned. Main St business district between W./E. Verona, W./E. West Jersey (jogs at Main) and W./E. Washington; Chestnut / S. 2nd St at top. W.J.&S. RR stations, Risley & Lake lumber yard, banks, theatre. Only 4 control points (2 street, 2 rail crossings).

sheet-6.description: North Main Street east of Washington Avenue, the civic and commercial core of Pleasantville, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. North Main Street crosses the sheet from left to right below the middle. West and East Washington Avenue form the left side, East and West Grant Avenue run beside the Philadelphia and Reading Railway (Atlantic City Division) in the middle, Old Turnpike leaves Main Street towards the bottom, and Pleasant Avenue forms the right side, with Linden Avenue leading off it. North 2nd Street, 1st Street and 1st Street (2nd Street) cross the upper half, and Madison Avenue runs along the bottom, where a trolley trestle crosses. The City Hall and fire department with lock-up stand on West Washington Avenue; near it are lodge halls above an office and upholstering shop, a garage for 75 autos, an undertaker, a club house, a printing shop and an auto repair shop. On Main Street are rows of brick and frame stores and the post office; south of it an ice cream factory with electric power, a plumber and the First Presbyterian Church on East Washington Avenue, and on Old Turnpike a blacksmith and wheelwright with printing and furniture storage. East of the railway a cement block works, a boarding house and rows of small brick and frame stores with numbered units stand among frame dwellings.
notes: Old West Grant Avenue lies on the line of today's Martin Luther King Jr Avenue near Main Street.
City Hall and fire department with lock-up; post office; First Presbyterian Church.
1st Street west of the railway and 1st Street (2nd Street) east of it are offset; today's North 1st Street joins them, so its junction with Martin Luther King Jr Avenue was excluded.

Single part, 50 ft, turned. N. Main St between W./E. Washington and Pleasant Av; W./E. Grant (W. Grant now MLK Jr Av) beside P&R Ry; Old Turnpike, Madison, 1st St. City Hall, post office, 1st Presbyterian Church.

sheet-7.description: Residential blocks on both sides of North Main Street north-east of the business district, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. North Main Street crosses the lower half of the sheet; 1st Street runs along the top, Linden Avenue across the upper half (offset at Lake Place, where the east part is also lettered Brisco) and Madison Avenue along the bottom. Pleasant Avenue forms the left side, Lake Place runs between 1st Street and Main Street, Taubel Avenue between Main Street and Madison Avenue, and West and East Adams Avenue form the right side; Charles Avenue is lettered below Madison Avenue. Most lots hold frame dwellings with auto houses and hen houses. Institutions are the Wesley M. E. Church (steam heat, electric light) at Pleasant and Linden Avenues, the Seventh Day Adventist Church on Lake Place and a W.C.T.U. hall. Main Street has a few stores, an auto repair shop, an auto sales room and a boarding house. The largest building is the vacant factory building of Taubel Scott Co. Inc. on Taubel Avenue, with hydrants and hose, a constant watchman and approved clock, and a heater room; a wagon shed stands behind Main Street east of Lake Place.
notes: Taubel Scott Co. Inc. vacant factory building.
Wesley M. E. Church; Seventh Day Adventist Church; W.C.T.U. hall.
Old Taubel Avenue between Main Street and Madison Avenue does not line up with today's Ingersoll Avenue; Ingersoll and Charles Avenue junctions were left out.

Single part, 50 ft, turned. N. Main between Pleasant Av and W./E. Adams; Lake Pl, Taubel Av, Linden (Brisco), 1st St, Madison. Wesley M.E. Church, 7th Day Adventist Church, Taubel Scott Co vacant factory.

sheet-8.description: The railroad and industrial strip north-west of the business district, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. South New Road runs along the top, South 4th Street and South 3rd Street cross the right half, and Spruce Street leads off to the right near the bottom; West Verona Avenue (Beaumont Avenue) forms the left side and West Washington Avenue the right side, with North New Road, North Fourth Street and North Third Street continuing beyond it. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad, electric and steam) runs straight down the middle of the sheet, and the Shore Fast Line of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad curves in from the left at the bottom, with a hand car house, a transformer house and sidings. Industrial premises include the Peerless Hosiery Dyeing Company (dye house, packing and shipping, boxing and boarding rooms, automatic sprinklers), Abbotts Alderney Dairies Inc. (wagon house, ice house, office), the Atlantic Foundry Company with foundry and pattern shop, a Sinclair Refining Company warehouse with gasoline tanks, the Lake and Bassler lumber and mill work yard with woodworking mill and lumber sheds, the Northfield Baking Company with ovens, a grain and feed warehouse, coal bins and storage buildings. Pleasantville High School (steam heat, electric light) occupies the block between South 3rd Street and Spruce Street on West Washington Avenue. Frame dwellings line South 4th and South 3rd Streets.
notes: Peerless Hosiery Dyeing Company; Abbotts Alderney Dairies Inc.; Atlantic Foundry Company; Sinclair Refining Company; Lake and Bassler lumber and mill work; Northfield Baking Company.
Pleasantville High School.
Placed on three junctions along West Washington Avenue and the South New Road crossing of today's Pleasantville Industrial Track; the West Verona Avenue side has no control of its own.
Today's West Jersey Avenue does not follow a street drawn on this sheet.

Single part, 50 ft, turned. P.R.R. (W.J.&S.) and Shore Fast Line between W. Verona (Beaumont) and W. Washington; S. New Road, S. 4th, S. 3rd. Peerless Hosiery Dyeing, Abbotts dairies, Atlantic Foundry, Lake & Bassler lumber, High School. Weak control: 3 points on one street plus 1 rail crossing.

sheet-9.description: Residential blocks north of the business district on either side of the Philadelphia and Reading Railway (Atlantic City Division), drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. West Washington Avenue forms the left side, with South Fourth, South Third and South Second Streets leading off it to the left; west of the railway North 4th Street, North 3rd Street, Spruce Street and North 2nd Street cross the sheet, and Brighton Place runs between Spruce Street and North 2nd Street. East of the railway the cross streets are numbered one higher in brackets: North 4th Street (5th Street), North 3rd Street (4th Street) and North 2nd Street (3rd Street), ending at Pleasant Avenue on the right side. The railway runs as a double track straight down the right-centre of the sheet with no buildings beside it. The blocks are almost entirely frame dwellings with auto houses, hen houses and sheds, a few with brick fronts; the only other uses are a store and service station with a gasoline tank at West Washington Avenue and North 4th Street and a printing shop with electric power on West Washington Avenue north of Spruce Street.
notes: The cross streets east of the railway carry an older number in brackets (North 4th Street was 5th Street, and so on); today they are North 4th, North 3rd and North 2nd Street.
Old Spruce Street is today's Vola Lane, which no longer follows the drawn line at West Washington Avenue (10.6 m; rejected).
The railway line is today's Martin Luther King Jr Avenue.

Single part, 50 ft, turned. W. Washington Av to Pleasant Av either side of P&R Ry (now MLK Jr Av); N. 4th, N. 3rd, Spruce (now Vola Ln), N. 2nd; east side streets numbered one higher in brackets. Dwellings.

sheet-10.description: Residential blocks north-west of the Main Street business district, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Pleasant Avenue runs down the left edge and West Adams Avenue down the right third of the sheet; between them North 4th Street (lettered 5th Street in brackets) runs along the top, North 3rd Street (4th Street) and North 2nd Street (3rd Street) cross the middle, and 1st Street (2nd Street) runs along the bottom edge. East of West Adams Avenue the cross streets are drawn offset from their continuations to the west, and a narrow strip of the next blocks to the east (sheet 19) is shown. The blocks are mostly long, deep lots, many still vacant or only partly built up, with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, auto houses, hen houses and a work shop; several dwellings are of concrete block. The largest buildings are the Wood-Wilson Mfg. Co. clothing factory at the corner of Pleasant Avenue and North 3rd Street (steam heat, electric light) and the 1st Baptist Church (hot air heat, electric light) on Pleasant Avenue near 1st Street. Four-inch water pipes are drawn along Pleasant Avenue, West Adams Avenue and 1st Street, with hydrants at the corners. House numbers are given with the older numbers in brackets. A scale of feet is printed in the lowest block.
notes: Cross streets carry their current names with the previous ones in brackets, one number higher (North 4th Street (5th Street), North 3rd Street (4th Street), North 2nd Street (3rd Street), 1st Street (2nd Street)); the main names match today's North 4th, 3rd, 2nd and 1st Street.
Wood-Wilson Mfg. Co. clothing factory at Pleasant Avenue and North 3rd Street.
1st Baptist Church on Pleasant Avenue near 1st Street.
Cross streets jog at West Adams Avenue; the modern street network has separate junctions on either side, 34 to 46 m apart.

Single part, 50 ft, turned (north upper right). Pleasant Av to W. Adams Av between N. 4th St (5th) and 1st St (2nd); cross streets lettered with old numbers one higher in brackets. Wood-Wilson Mfg. Co. clothing factory, 1st Baptist Church.

sheet-11-1.description: The bay front at the south end of the city, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. South Edgeley Avenue runs along the top; below it East Greenfield, East Oakland, East Edgewater and East Bayview Avenues run down the sheet to the shore of Lakes Bay, which fills the lower part. Three canals, 20 ft wide, are cut between the avenues from the bay up to about the middle of the blocks, and a fourth, short canal enters beside East Bayview Avenue. The canal blocks are platted in narrow lots and only lightly built up, mostly with small one- and one-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings, boat houses and a few vending stands; many cottages carry names, among them Bayview Cottage, Ogden Cottage, Arcadia, Seldom Inn, Major Cottage, Shamrock, Idle Hour, Marsh Cottage, Dixie, Marigold, Pinafore, Lu Lu, Keystone, Fairview, Rexall, Seaside, Bay View and Restless Cottage. The boundary between the City of Pleasantville and Egg Harbor Township crosses the blocks diagonally. East of East Bayview Avenue a large unbuilt tract (block 73) is crossed only by property lines, and in the upper right corner a strip shows Tunis Avenue and East Decatur Avenue where they meet South Franklin Avenue and South Chester Avenue, continuing sheet 2. A heavy line encloses the lower right quarter, which is drawn as a separate part (the blocks along Atlantic City Boulevard). Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn along the avenues.
notes: Old East Oakland Avenue is Oakland Avenue today; old South Franklin Avenue is South Franklin Boulevard and old South Chester Avenue is South Hampden Court.

Tunis Avenue north of South Franklin Avenue is drawn in line with its southern part; the modern street there is about 30 m to the west, so its junctions with South Edgeley Avenue and South Franklin Boulevard were left out.
Ansley Boulevard, Roosevelt Drive and East Wright Street, which today cross the canal blocks and block 73, are not drawn.
Control is thin: three junctions along South Edgeley Avenue and two in the upper right strip; the canal blocks towards the bay have none.

Two parts, 100 ft. Part 1 main: canal blocks between E. Greenfield, E. Oakland, E. Edgewater, E. Bayview Avs on Lakes Bay below S. Edgeley Av, plus Tunis/E. Decatur strip; city/Egg Harbor Twp line; control only along the top. Part 2: inset (heavy line, lower right) Atlantic City Blvd (now E. Verona Av) between Tunis and E. West Jersey Av, S. Lyons Ct to Florence Av (cross streets named one block off from today).

sheet-11-2.description: An inset in the lower right quarter of sheet 11, enclosed by a heavy line, showing the blocks east of sheet 2 on either side of Atlantic City Boulevard, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned like the rest of the atlas so that north points to the upper right. Tunis Avenue runs down the left side, Atlantic City Boulevard (80 ft wide) down the middle and East West Jersey Avenue, with the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) beside it, down the right edge. They are crossed, from top to bottom, by South Lyons Court, Frankfort Court, Toulon Avenue, Genoa Avenue, Palermo Avenue and Florence Avenue. Only the blocks west of the boulevard and next to South Lyons Court are partly built up, with one- and one-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings and auto houses; a gasoline filling station with its tanks stands at Atlantic City Boulevard and South Lyons Court. The blocks further east and south (252 to 255, 259 to 261) are platted into lots but empty. Six-inch water pipes are drawn along Tunis Avenue, Frankfort Court, Toulon Avenue and the boulevard, and a narrow strip of the canal area of the main map shows to the left of the dividing line.
notes: The cross streets are named one block off from today's names: old South Lyons Court is Frankfort Avenue, old Frankfort Court is Toulon Avenue, old Toulon Avenue is Genoa Avenue, old Genoa Avenue is Palermo Avenue, old Palermo Avenue is Florence Avenue and old Florence Avenue is Cordova Avenue.
Old Atlantic City Boulevard is East Verona Avenue (Black Horse Pike) today; East West Jersey Avenue continues as Milan Avenue south of Genoa Avenue.
East West Jersey Avenue is drawn about 40 ft wide against about 65 ft of right-of-way today; street_widths was set to 40 ft.
Tunis Avenue is drawn straight; the modern road (Tunis Avenue and Bay Drive) curves away, so its junctions were not used.
Gasoline filling station at Atlantic City Boulevard and South Lyons Court.

Two parts, 100 ft. Part 1 main: canal blocks between E. Greenfield, E. Oakland, E. Edgewater, E. Bayview Avs on Lakes Bay below S. Edgeley Av, plus Tunis/E. Decatur strip; city/Egg Harbor Twp line; control only along the top. Part 2: inset (heavy line, lower right) Atlantic City Blvd (now E. Verona Av) between Tunis and E. West Jersey Av, S. Lyons Ct to Florence Av (cross streets named one block off from today).

sheet-12.description: North Main Street north-east of the centre, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. North Main Street crosses the upper half of the sheet from West and East Adams Avenues on the left to Loraine Avenue on the right; Linden Avenue (lettered Brisco at its west end and 1st Street further east) runs along the top and North Franklin Avenue crosses the lower half. The cross streets are, from left to right, West and East Adams Avenues, Woodland and East Woodland Avenues (East Woodland continuing south as Collins Avenue), West and East Merion Avenues, West and East Greenway Avenues and West and East Mulberry Avenues, with North Edgeley Avenue and a second, eastern stretch of North Franklin Avenue between Greenway and Loraine Avenues. Madison Avenue ends at East Adams Avenue on the left. The blocks along Main Street and north of it are built up with frame dwellings, a few stores and an office; the larger buildings are the Pleasantville Public School No. 1 (steam heat, electric light) between West Adams and Woodland Avenues, the Nickerson Apartments on Woodland Avenue, the Faith Tabernacle on West Merion Avenue and a silk mill (electric power and light, steam heat) at West Mulberry Avenue. South of North Franklin Avenue the blocks are platted in long narrow lots, many with 20 ft alleys, and are mostly empty; the boundary line between the City of Pleasantville and Egg Harbor Township runs along the bottom of the sheet.
notes: Pleasantville Public School No. 1; Faith Tabernacle; Nickerson Apartments; silk mill at West Mulberry Avenue.

Old North Franklin Avenue is North Franklin Boulevard today west of East Merion Avenue; its eastern stretch near East Mulberry and Loraine Avenues does not match the modern road, and those junctions were left out.
West and East Greenway Avenues are gone; the Atlantic City Expressway now crosses the sheet along their line.
The junctions of Linden Avenue with Woodland Avenue and of East Mulberry Avenue with North Edgeley Avenue were detected about 12 m off the fit and rejected.

Single part, 100 ft. N. Main St from W./E. Adams to Loraine Av, Linden Av (1st St) to N. Franklin Av; Public School No. 1, Nickerson Apts, Faith Tabernacle, silk mill. Greenway Avs now under the Atlantic City Expressway.

sheet-13.description: North Main Street at the north end of the city, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right, at a slightly different angle from the sheets further south. North Main Street crosses the middle of the sheet from Loraine Avenue on the left to West and East Delilah Road on the right. Linden Avenue (1st Street) runs across the upper part and Florence Avenue along the top right; North Franklin Avenue crosses the lower middle between East Reading Avenue and Stenton Place. The cross streets are, from left to right, Loraine Avenue, Brighton Avenue, Wellington Avenue (at the top), Walnut Avenue, West and East Reading Avenue, Chatham Avenue, Stenton Place, West and East Windsor Avenue and West and East Delilah Road. Main Street is lined with frame dwellings and a few stores, a bakery near Brighton Avenue and an office near Chatham Avenue; the Mt. Pleasant M. E. Church (electric light, furnace heat) stands at Main Street and West Reading Avenue. Hen houses, coops and a pump house occupy the deep back lots, and a hollow tile brick works appears both north of Linden Avenue and on East Reading Avenue, where a building is marked not completed, work stopped. South of North Franklin Avenue and Main Street the blocks are long and largely empty, and the boundary between the City of Pleasantville and Egg Harbor Township runs along the bottom of the sheet.
notes: Mt. Pleasant M. E. Church at North Main Street and West Reading Avenue.
Hollow tile brick manufacturing on East Reading Avenue and north of Linden Avenue; one building marked not completed, work stopped.
The fitted rotation (about 60 degrees) differs by about 4 degrees from sheets 2 to 12.

Modern North Franklin Boulevard continues west of East Reading Avenue and east of Stenton Place where the sheet draws no street; those junctions were left out. The Chatham Avenue junctions were detected 8 to 14 m off the fit and rejected.
Single part, 100 ft, rotation about 60. N. Main St from Loraine Av to W./E. Delilah Rd; Mt. Pleasant M. E. Church, hollow tile brick works.

sheet-14.description: North Main Street at the north end of the city, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with Main Street running straight up the sheet, so that north points to the upper left (the sheet is turned differently from the southern sheets). The cross streets run slightly uphill to the right: from top to bottom a Private Way, West and East Leeds Avenue, Princeton Avenue (lettered Blemheim in brackets), West and East Lindley Avenue, West and East Thompson Avenue, Pacific Avenue, Atlantic Avenue and West and East Delilah Road. East of Main Street, Franklin Avenue (1st Street) runs between Leeds and Princeton Avenues, Iowa Avenue from Utah Avenue down to Princeton Avenue, and Pennsylvania Avenue (Bayview) runs along the top right. The blocks east of Main Street are platted in long rows of narrow lots and only lightly built up with one- and two-storey frame dwellings and auto houses; west of Main Street the lots are deeper, with dwellings, stores, stables and lumber piles near Delilah Road. Large tracts (201 and 207) north of Leeds Avenue are open. The Atlantic City water works mains (20 and 30 inch) cross the upper left part of the sheet beside the Private Way, with an emergency 8-inch connection to Main Street, and the Atlantic City Water Department supply mains cross the right-hand blocks near Iowa Avenue. A concrete block garage for twelve cars stands on Main Street north of Leeds Avenue. The boundary between the City of Pleasantville and Egg Harbor Township runs along the right edge.
notes: Atlantic City Water Works mains cross the sheet; emergency 8-inch connection to the 20-inch mains of the Atlantic City Water Works at Main Street.
Old Franklin Avenue (1st Street) is North Franklin Boulevard today.

Modern Iowa Avenue continues south of Princeton Avenue, where the sheet draws none; its junction with Pacific Avenue was detected 15 m off and rejected, and those with Lindley and Thompson Avenues were left out.
Atlantic Avenue does not survive on its 1924 line; Delilah Road junctions at the bottom edge were not detected.
Control lies in the left and upper parts of the sheet; the blocks south of Lindley Avenue east of Main Street have none.
Single part, 100 ft, turned with Main St running up the sheet (rotation about -35). N. Main St from Private Way to Delilah Rd, Leeds to Pacific Avs, Iowa Av; Atlantic City water mains, 12-car garage.

sheet-15.description: The northern edge of the city, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with North Main Street running up the left side, so that north points to the upper left. The boundary between the City of Pleasantville and the City of Absecon follows West California Avenue on the left and then runs above Nevada Avenue across the top; the boundary with Egg Harbor Township runs down the right edge. East of Main Street a grid of blocks (211 to 221) is laid out between East California Avenue and East Redwood Avenue and up to Nevada Avenue, crossed by 8th Avenue, Boulevard, 7th Avenue and Ocean Avenue; the blocks are platted into lots but only a few one- to two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings, auto houses and a foundation stand on them. West of Main Street, between West California and Magnolia Avenues on either side of West Redwood Avenue and Longshore Avenue, the Atlantic Summer Colony is drawn with a row of camp cottages and a garage for twenty cars (cement floor, electric light, stove heat) on Main Street. Below Redwood Avenue a large open tract (block 210) is crossed by the line of Boice Avenue, drawn dashed as not opened, and Cedarcrest Avenue runs across the lower part of the sheet to Iowa Avenue and Pennsylvania Avenue (Bayview), where the blocks of sheet 14 begin. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run along Main Street, Nevada Avenue and Boulevard.
notes: Atlantic Summer Colony with camp cottages and a 20-car garage on Main Street.
Old Boulevard is North Franklin Boulevard today.
Boice Avenue is drawn dashed as not opened; the modern streets laid out over block 210 (Stuart Place, Larchmont Drive, Bellevue Parkway, Montclaire Drive) are not drawn.

Modern Redwood Avenue east of Boulevard and Longshore Drive do not follow the drawn streets; their junctions were left out. Nevada Avenue was not used because the modern junction names there could not be matched with confidence.

Single part, 100 ft, rotation about -34. North edge: E. California to Redwood Avs, 8th Av, Boulevard (N. Franklin Blvd), 7th, Ocean Avs; Atlantic Summer Colony cottages; Boice Av not opened; Absecon city line.

sheet-16-1.description: South Main Street at the south-west edge of the city, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. South Main Street crosses the sheet in its middle and Broad Street runs parallel above it; along the top runs the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad, the Shore Fast Line, electric and steam), with a short street lettered Not Named and Ashland Avenue in the margin above. The cross streets are Tilton Road, Floral Avenue, Fernwood Avenue (not opened north of Broad Street), Tremont Avenue and Glendale Avenue, with Maple Avenue (not opened) and Plaza Place south of Main Street. The left edge follows the line between the City of Pleasantville and Northfield, with a note to see the map of Northfield. West of Tilton Road lies the Collins Farm with long pigeon houses, sheds and dwellings; between Tilton Road and Floral Avenue north of Broad Street is a base ball park with a grand stand. The blocks between Floral and Glendale Avenues and along Main Street are built up with one- to two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings, auto houses and a plumbing shop; the blocks north of Broad Street are platted in narrow lots with 20 ft alleys. A heavy line encloses the lower right of the sheet, which is a separate inset (part 2) showing the Atlantic City Water Department pumping station near Leeds Avenue.
notes: West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad), Shore Fast Line, electric and steam, along the top; the line is now a trail (Pleasantville to Somers Point) and was not used for control.
Base ball park with grand stand; Collins Farm with pigeon houses.
Old Maple Avenue (not opened) is East Ridgewood Avenue today; old Floral Avenue is West Floral Avenue and old Glendale Avenue is West Glendale Avenue.
The fitted rotation (about 51 degrees) differs from sheets 2 to 12 (about 64).
The inset in the lower right (part 2, the pumping station on Leeds Avenue) has no street junction and was not georeferenced.

Two parts, 100 ft, rotation about 51. Part 1 main: S. Main and Broad St between Tilton Rd and Glendale Av; base ball park, Collins Farm pigeon houses, W.J.&S. RR at top. Part 2: inset (heavy line, lower right) Atlantic City Water Dept. pumping station and Public School No. 3 on Leeds Av; no junction, not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Atlantic City Water Dept. pumping station and Public School No. 3 on Leeds Avenue (no street junction; needs step 6b, points carried from sheet-14 (blocks 193A and 201, Private Way, water mains)).

sheet-17.description: South Main Street south-west of the centre, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Shore Fast Line, electric and steam) runs along the top with Smith's Landing Station; Broad Street (90 ft) crosses the upper half, bending to the north-east beyond Willard Avenue, and South Main Street crosses the middle. North of Main Street the cross streets are Glendale, Shadeland, West Park, Willard, Maple and West Greenfield Avenues; south of it Frambious, Ryon, East Park and East Greenfield Avenues run down to Clematis Avenue and Narcissus Avenue (not opened) near the bottom, with Prospect Avenue, East Oakland Avenue and Edgeley Avenue in the lower right. A stretch of Broad Street east of West Park Avenue is marked not opened. The blocks are residential, with one- to two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings and auto houses, and a row of stores on Main Street near Willard Avenue. Notable buildings are Smith's Landing Public School No. 2 (steam heat, gas and electric light) and the Morrison Concrete Products Co. Inc. works making concrete blocks, both beside the railroad, and the Salem M. E. Church (steam heat, electric light) on Main Street between West Park and Willard Avenues. Salem Cemetery occupies the block between West Park and Maple Avenues north of Broad Street.
notes: Smith's Landing Station on the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad; Smith's Landing Public School No. 2.
Morrison Concrete Products Co. Inc., concrete block works.
Salem M. E. Church on South Main Street.
Old Frambious Avenue is Frambes Avenue today.

Modern West and East Greenfield Avenues are about 45 m from the drawn Greenfield Avenue at Main Street and were not used; Broad Street junctions east of Shadeland Avenue and Main Street at Shadeland and Frambious Avenues were detected 6 to 13 m off and were excluded.
Fitted scale is about 3 percent smaller than 100 ft to an inch (3.85 px per ft against about 3.96 on neighbouring sheets).

Single part, 100 ft (fits about 3 percent small), rotation about 48. S. Main and Broad St from Glendale to W. Greenfield Av, Clematis and Narcissus Avs below; Smith's Landing station and Public School No. 2, Morrison Concrete Products, Salem M. E. Church and cemetery. Weak geometric agreement; 7 points.

sheet-18.description: Blocks west and south of the Main Street business district, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Marple Avenue and South New Road run along the top, Fairview Avenue and Portland Avenue lie below them, and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Shore Fast Line, electric and steam) crosses the upper half diagonally with a curved branch at the right. Broad Street and Chestnut Street cross the middle, South Main Street runs diagonally across the lower half and Prospect Avenue and South Edgeley Avenue cross the bottom. The cross streets are, from left to right, West Greenfield, West and East Edgewater, West and East Bayview, West and East Wright, Sheffield and West and East Decatur Avenues, with West and East Verona Avenue (Beaumont Avenue) along the right edge and East Oakland Avenue at the lower left. Industry lies along the railroad: the McAllister Coal Co. coal pocket with four silos, coal sheds and a scale, the Lake and Risley Co. cement block storage, the American Ice Co. and, at the top right, Risley's Empire Laundry with the Peerless Plush Mfg. Co. Institutions include the Mt. Zion Baptist Church on Marple Avenue, the Grand Samaritan Temple, the Asbury M. E. Church on Broad Street, School No. 4 near Sheffield Avenue and St. Peter's Roman Catholic Church on Chestnut Street at West Verona Avenue. Byrd's Hotel stands on Wright Avenue; South Main Street near Decatur Avenue has stores, a garage and a parking area. Elsewhere the blocks hold frame dwellings and auto houses.
notes: McAllister Coal Co. coal pocket with silos on the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad; Lake and Risley Co. cement block storage; American Ice Co.
Risley's Empire Laundry and Peerless Plush Mfg. Co.
Mt. Zion Baptist Church; Asbury M. E. Church; Grand Samaritan Temple; St. Peter's Roman Catholic Church; School No. 4; Byrd's Hotel.

Old Chestnut Street is Chestnut Street South today; old West and East Wright Avenue are West and East Wright Street; old West Verona Avenue (Beaumont Avenue) is now the Black Horse Pike and was not used.
The railroad is now a trail and was not used for control. Oakland Avenue at South Main Street was detected 12 m off and rejected.

Single part, 100 ft. Marple Av to S. Edgeley Av between W. Greenfield and W. Verona (Beaumont) Avs; McAllister Coal Co., Risley's Empire Laundry, Peerless Plush, School No. 4, St. Peter's R.C., Asbury M.E. Church.

sheet-19.description: Residential district north-west of the town centre, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. North New Road crosses the top of the sheet and Linden Avenue (also lettered 1st Street) the bottom, with a jog where it meets Woodland Avenue. Woodland Avenue runs diagonally up the left half from Linden Avenue to North New Road; west of it the numbered cross streets (North 4th, North 3rd, North 2nd and 1st Street, each lettered with an older number in brackets) run to the left edge, where the sheet adjoins sheets 24, 10 and 7. Merion Avenue, West Greenway Avenue, West Mulberry Avenue and Brighton Avenue run up the right half, with short pieces of North 3rd and North 2nd Street between them; a short second piece of West Mulberry Avenue leaves Linden Avenue to the south-west of the main one. In the top left corner Mill Road and Oneida Avenue bound a row of narrow lots. The district is thinly built: frame dwellings, many with hen houses and auto houses, on long narrow lots, with large open blocks (165, 171, 175) still unsubdivided. The few other buildings are a small concrete-block garage near North New Road, a storage building, a six-car garage with a pump station off Woodland Avenue, a small shop on North 2nd Street, greenhouses between Woodland and Merion Avenues, and oil tanks east of Merion Avenue. Water pipes are drawn in North New Road, Woodland Avenue, North 2nd Street and Linden Avenue. The sheet carries the compass rose, the Sanborn title cartouche (Sept. 1924, Pleasantville N.J.) and the scale bar.
notes: The numbered cross streets carry an older number in brackets (North 4th Street was 5th Street, and so on; Linden Avenue was 1st Street).

Old North 2nd Street east of Woodland Avenue and the unnamed street north from it are today's Cedar Avenue; old West Greenway Avenue has no modern counterpart (the Atlantic City Expressway now crosses the sheet near it).
Old North 4th Street east of the left-hand blocks is drawn bent towards North New Road; today's North 4th Street runs straight to Woodland Avenue about 14 m away, so that junction was left out.
Linden Avenue jogs at Woodland Avenue, on the sheet and today; the junction was left out (hand-picked points on either side disagreed with the fit by 8 to 9 m).
Placed on 11 points; the two North New Road junctions carry 4.6 to 4.7 m residuals.

Single part, 100 ft. Residential NW of centre: Woodland, Merion, W. Greenway, W. Mulberry, Brighton Avs between N. New Rd and Linden Av; cross streets lettered with older numbers in brackets. Top third weak.

sheet-20.description: Thinly built district on the north-west edge of Pleasantville, north of sheet 19, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. North New Road crosses the top of the sheet and Linden Avenue the bottom; Brighton Avenue forms the left side and West Delilah Road the right. Between them Wellington Avenue and West Reading Avenue run the full height of the sheet, Gladstone Avenue and Oxford Avenue cross between Wellington and West Reading near the bottom, and a short piece of North 3rd Street (dashed, not built through) and 2nd Street cross near Brighton Avenue. North of North New Road the ends of Trenton, Reading, Richmond and Windsor Avenues are drawn with the first lots of blocks 167 to 170; Richmond and Windsor Avenues continue a short way south of the road. Large parts of the sheet are open land divided into big blocks (177, 178, 178A); St. Charles Place and 2nd Street east of West Delilah Road are lettered not open, and St. Charles Place is already laid out in narrow lots. Buildings are scattered frame dwellings with auto houses, hen houses and poultry houses, a few of concrete block or tile. At the corner of Brighton Avenue and North New Road stands a store with gasoline tanks, an auto repair shop and a 30 ft tower. In the middle of block 178A a dwelling has greenhouses, a work shop and a row of poultry houses. Water pipes are drawn in Wellington Avenue, West Reading Avenue, West Delilah Road and Linden Avenue.
notes: St. Charles Place and 2nd Street east of West Delilah Road are lettered not open.

Old Gladstone Avenue is today's Stratford Avenue, about 7 m off the drawn line; its junctions were left out. Old 2nd Street east of West Delilah Road is today's Homer Avenue; old North 3rd Street at Brighton Avenue is Balfour Avenue.
West Reading Avenue jogs at North New Road (Trenton Avenue continues north of the road on a line west of it); today's West Reading Avenue runs straight through, so that junction was left out.
Single part, 100 ft. NW edge: Brighton, Wellington, W. Reading Avs, W. Delilah Rd between N. New Rd and Linden Av; Gladstone, Oxford, Florence Avs; St. Charles Pl not open.

sheet-21.description: Residential addition at the south-west edge of Pleasantville, along the boundary with Northfield, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right; the street grid here lies at a different angle from the town centre. Tilton Road runs up the left side of the built area, with the city line and a note referring to the map of Northfield beyond it; the strip west of Tilton Road holds only a few scattered dwellings and a small restaurant on South New Road. South New Road crosses the sheet diagonally. Ashland, Fernwood, Tremont and Glendale Avenues run up the sheet, crossed by Jefferson, Harrison, Columbia and McKinley Avenues and, at the bottom, an unnamed street between Tilton Road and Ashland Avenue. Along the bottom edge runs the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad Shore Fast Line (electric and steam). The blocks are numbered 16 to 32 and are laid out in narrow lots, about half built on with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, auto houses, coops and a few stores, mostly near South New Road and McKinley Avenue. Institutions are two buildings of the Mt. Pleasant Baptist Church (one moved from Plains) on Columbia Avenue near Fernwood Avenue and the S.A.M.E. Church on Harrison Avenue; a wood-sawing shed stands on Columbia Avenue. The upper right corner (block 18) is left blank. Water pipes are drawn in South New Road, Columbia, McKinley, Fernwood, Tremont and Glendale Avenues.
notes: The unnamed street at the bottom between Tilton Road and Ashland Avenue is today's Langston Avenue; Ashland Avenue is today's West Ashland Avenue.
The West Jersey and Seashore Shore Fast Line along the bottom edge is today the Pleasantville to Somers Point bike path.
South New Road / West Ashland Avenue was rejected (12.8 m): South New Road does not meet Ashland Avenue on today's line. Columbia / Glendale Avenue, on the right edge, was left out.
Mt. Pleasant Baptist Church (two buildings, one lettered moved from Plains); S.A.M.E. Church.
Single part, 100 ft, rotation about 51. SW addition on Tilton Rd at the Northfield line: Ashland, Fernwood, Tremont, Glendale x Jefferson, Harrison, Columbia, McKinley; Shore Fast Line along bottom.

sheet-22.description: South-west part of Pleasantville between sheet 21 and the West Jersey and Seashore Shore Fast Line, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. South New Road crosses the middle of the sheet. West Park Avenue runs down the left half from Harrison Avenue across South New Road to the railway; Doughty Road runs diagonally from the bottom centre up to the right across South New Road; Noahs Road runs north from South New Road to its crossing with Church Road in the upper right; West Bayview Avenue forms the right edge, with Maple Avenue leaving it eastward. On the left, Glendale Avenue is crossed by Harrison, Columbia and McKinley Avenues and an alley, and Shadeland Avenue runs from McKinley Avenue to the railway. Portland Avenue runs from Doughty Road to West Bayview Avenue in the lower right; below the railway the ends of Maple, West Greenfield and West Edgewater Avenues are drawn. The upper half is mostly open land (block 48), with a few dwellings along West Park Avenue and on Noahs Road. The built blocks hold one- and two-storey frame dwellings with auto houses, hen houses and a few stores; a dwelling on Portland Avenue is marked under construction. The one industrial site is the Standard Oil Co. bulk station beside the railway on Shadeland Avenue: oil and gasoline tanks, an oil pump station and a canning house. Water pipes are drawn in South New Road, West Park Avenue, Glendale and McKinley Avenues, Doughty Road, Portland Avenue and West Bayview Avenue.
notes: Standard Oil Co. bulk station with oil pump station and canning house beside the railway.
Old Church Road is today's Church Street; the alley south of McKinley Avenue is McKinley Place.
The railway along the bottom edge (the West Jersey and Seashore Shore Fast Line) is today the Pleasantville to Somers Point bike path.
Single part, 100 ft, rotation about 47. SW: W. Park Av, Doughty, Noahs, Church Rds, S. New Rd, Glendale/Shadeland, Portland Av, W. Bayview; Standard Oil bulk station.

sheet-23.description: South-western part of Pleasantville between South New Road and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. In the upper left, Church Road and Noah's Road enclose a small grid of Ohio, New Jersey and Risley Avenues (blocks 49A to 49C); the two roads cross below it, Noah's Road continuing to the left edge. Doughty Road runs diagonally from South New Road at the left edge across the whole sheet to the railway in the upper right. South New Road crosses the lower left, meeting Doughty Road, Church Road and West Bayview Avenue at a five-way junction, and turns down towards Marple Avenue at the bottom; Wright Street and West Bayview Avenue run between South New Road and Marple Avenue. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad, electric and steam) runs up the right side. Most of the right half is open land: the large block 46 north of Doughty Road and a cemetery (block 54) to the south of it. Housing is frame dwellings with auto houses and coops, densest in the upper left and along Doughty Road; a few stores stand near the five-way junction. Named buildings are St. John's M.E. Church on Church Road, a carpet cleaning works at the top left, and the O.J. Hammell Co. monumental works by the railway (stone cutting, blacksmith shop and storage). Across the railway are a chapel and receiving vault of the adjoining cemetery, drawn as an exposure. Water pipes are drawn in South New Road, Doughty Road, West Bayview Avenue and Marple Avenue.
notes: O.J. Hammell Co. monumental works (power and lights electric); St. John's M.E. Church; carpet cleaning works.
Old Church Road is today's Church Street; Wright Street is West Wright Street.
All control lies in the left half; the open blocks and cemetery on the right are placed by extrapolation. The Doughty Road crossing of today's Pleasantville Industrial Track was rejected (4.6 m).

Single part, 100 ft, rotation about 69. SW: Church and Noah's Rds, Ohio/New Jersey/Risley Avs, Doughty Rd, S. New Rd, W. Bayview, Wright, Marple; cemetery; O.J. Hammell monumental works by the W.J.&S. RR. Control in left half only.

sheet-24.description: North-western part of Pleasantville on both sides of the Philadelphia and Reading Railway, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. North New Road crosses the bottom of the sheet, continuing west as South New Road, and North 4th Street (also lettered 5th Street) runs along the bottom edge, with South Fourth Street at the lower left. The railway runs diagonally up the middle. West of it, West Washington Avenue runs up the left side past a large cemetery (block 96, with a chapel), with a second cemetery lettered beyond it; Lehigh Avenue and Clinton Avenue (not open) cross at the top, and Ireland Avenue, Brad Street and Fellows Avenue form the built blocks 97 and 98 near North New Road. East of the railway, Pleasant Avenue runs up from North 4th Street, and Wesley, West Adams and Oneida Avenues run the full height of the sheet, crossed by Chalfonte, Belmont and Gladstone Avenues; Mill Road leaves West Adams Avenue towards the lower right. The large block 110 beside the railway is open land. Housing is one- and two-storey frame dwellings with auto houses, coops and some concrete-block buildings, on narrow lots; a store and greenhouse stand at West Washington Avenue and North New Road, and a confectionery works at the railway on North New Road. Industrial buildings are the Atlantic Co. Light and Power Co. substation by the railway (engine room, transformer house, boilers not used) and two concrete block works on Gladstone Avenue. Water pipes are drawn in North and South New Road, North 4th Street, West Washington Avenue and Pleasant Avenue.
notes: Clinton Avenue is lettered not open.
Atlantic Co. Light and Power Co. substation (boilers not used); two concrete block works; a confectionery works on North New Road.
The Philadelphia and Reading Railway line is today's Martin Luther King Jr Avenue; its junctions were not used.
Single part, 100 ft. NW both sides of the P.&R. Ry: W. Washington Av and cemetery; Pleasant, Wesley, W. Adams, Oneida x Chalfonte, Belmont, Gladstone; Atlantic Co. Light & Power substation.

sheet-25.description: Residential subdivision on the north-west edge of Pleasantville, north of sheet 19 and east of sheet 24, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Oneida, Seneca, Cayuga, Woodland and Spruce Avenues run up the sheet in a regular grid, crossed by Islesworth, Chalfonte and Belmont Avenues; Mill Road crosses the lower part of the sheet diagonally, and West Mulberry Avenue (partly dashed) leaves it in the lower right. North of Islesworth Avenue the lots fan out along curved streets: Seneca Avenue ends in a small circle, and Glenwood Avenue and the curving north ends of Woodland and Spruce Avenues are laid out in radiating lots (blocks 137 to 144). The blocks are almost entirely platted but little built: scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings, auto houses, hen houses and a dwelling with an auto house in a cement cellar, mostly on Oneida, Seneca and Woodland Avenues and along Mill Road. East of Spruce Avenue are large undivided tracts (blocks 164 and 165), with a no-exposure note along the right edge. Water pipes are drawn in Woodland and Spruce Avenues and Chalfonte Avenue.
notes: Old Cayuga Avenue has no junctions in today's street data; it was not used for control.
All control lies west of Spruce Avenue; the open tracts east of it are placed by extrapolation (first-order fit set on purpose).
Single part, 100 ft. NW subdivision: Oneida, Seneca, Cayuga, Woodland, Spruce x Islesworth, Chalfonte, Belmont, Mill Rd; radiating lots on Glenwood Av.

sheet-26.description: North-western edge of Pleasantville astride the Philadelphia and Reading Railway, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. The boundary between the City of Pleasantville and Egg Harbor Township crosses the upper half of the sheet as a dash-dot line; above it the sheet is blank except for the Standard Bitulithic Co. asphalt plant beside a railway spur in the upper right (crude oil and asphalt tanks, stone crushers, asphalt kettle, a gasoline-engine pump house, a coal trestle on concrete piers, office and scales). West Washington Avenue runs up the left of the city part, with Billie Place leaving it westward; Doughty Road crosses diagonally from the lower left to the railway, which runs from the bottom centre to the upper right. Between them lie a short street lettered Adams with platted lots (block 90A), the open block 90, and blocks 92 to 94 on Indiana, Cambria and Sommerset Avenues. East of the railway, Wesley and West Adams Avenues are crossed by Islesworth Avenue, the continuation of Sommerset Avenue. Housing is frame dwellings with auto houses, coops and a few stores, densest along Cambria and Sommerset Avenues; a hand laundry stands on Cambria Avenue. West of West Washington Avenue are vacant buildings, hen houses and a concrete block works. The area beyond the left edge is noted as vacant.
notes: Standard Bitulithic Co. asphalt plant (watchman, no clock) beyond the city line; a concrete block works and a hand laundry.
Old Billie Place is today's Devins Lane (hand-picked: drawn 18 ft wide); old Sommerset Avenue is today's Somerset Avenue. Indiana Avenue has no modern counterpart in the street data.
Placed on six points, all in the lower half; the area beyond the city line, including the asphalt plant, is placed by extrapolation.
